facts.claim: As at November 2026, smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (last updated 18 August 2026): you can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if valid where it happened and valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia; talk to a lawyer to confirm. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.
facts.quote: You can't register an overseas marriage in Australia. But in most cases, your marriage is legally recognised here. To be recognised, when you got married it must have been: valid under the law of the country where it happened; valid under Australian law if it had occurred in Australia. ... Talk to a lawyer to confirm your overseas marriage certificate is valid in Australia.

facts.claim: [Copied from is-marriage-in-italy-recognised-in-australia 03-source-pack fact_01, same source and date.] Smartraveller (last updated Tuesday 18/08/2026): 'You can't register an overseas marriage in Australia. But in most cases, your marriage is legally recognised here. To be recognised, when you got married it must have been: valid under the law of the country where it happened; valid under Australian law if it had occurred in Australia.'

[Copied from is-marriage-in-italy-recognised-in-australia 03-source-pack fact_25, same source and date.] Smartraveller: 'A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage. But you may be unable to use it as proof of a name change. Find out from your local registry of births, deaths and marriages.'

[Copied from same-sex-marriage-greece 03-source-pack fact_106, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 12 November 2026): some countries ask you to prove you aren't already married; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages; the country may have more rules (for example a residence period); 'We can't tell you what you will need'; contact your destination's embassy or consulate. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

[Copied from same-sex-marriage-greece 03-source-pack fact_107, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (read live 12 November 2026): your registry of births, deaths and marriages can give a statement that there's no record you have been married before, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate; local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, the death certificate of a deceased spouse, and your original birth certificate and passport.

[Copied from same-sex-marriage-greece 03-source-pack fact_115 (originally mykonos-wedding part-1 fact_101), same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, the Attorney-General's Department 'Get married' page (read live 23 November 2026), under 'Get married overseas': 'Overseas marriages cannot be: performed by an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant; registered in Australia.' 'An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it: was a valid marriage in the overseas country; would have been a valid marriage here.' 'You may be able to use your overseas marriage certificate to prove that you got married. However, some states and territories don't accept overseas marriage certificates if you want to change your name.' The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, the Junta Central Electoral help centre article '¿Cuáles son los requisitos para un matrimonio civil?' (read live 24 November 2026; 'Created: 10/18/2014', 'Modified: 7/1/2025'), for foreigners ('En el caso de los extranjeros'): 'Acta de nacimiento', 'Pasaporte.', 'Constancia de soltería instrumentada en el país de origen.' Paraphrase: foreigners provide a birth certificate, passport and a certificate of single status issued in their country of origin. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026): 'En el caso de los extranjeros, toda documentación que presenten deberá estar legalizada y apostillada del país de origen. En caso de que se trate de un país que no sea signatario del Convenio de la Apostilla de La Haya, se debe legalizar por la autoridad consular dominicana acreditada al lugar donde fue expedida.' Paraphrase: all documents foreigners present must be legalised and apostilled in the country of origin; from a non-Hague Apostille country, legalised by the Dominican consular authority accredited where issued. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026): 'Si el documento no está escrito en castellano, debe ser traducido por un intérprete judicial y legalizado por la Procuraduría General de la República. En algunos casos la traducción puede ser hecha en el mismo Consulado Dominicano, en este caso el documento debe ser legalizado en el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Cancillería).' Paraphrase: documents not in Spanish must be translated by a judicial interpreter and legalised by the Attorney General's Office (Procuraduría General de la República); in some cases the translation can be done at the Dominican consulate, in which case it is legalised at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026): 'Algunas Delegaciones Diplomáticas acreditadas en territorio dominicano reciben la declaración de soltería de sus ciudadanos.' Paraphrase: some diplomatic missions accredited in the Dominican Republic take single-status declarations from their own citizens. (Whether any mission does this for Australians is not stated.)

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026), item 5: 'Dos (2) testigos por lo menos, los cuales podrán ser familiares o no de los contrayentes, siempre que sean mayores de edad, que sepan firmar y porten cédula de identidad o cédula de identidad y electoral o pasaporte vigente en el caso de los extranjeros.' Paraphrase: at least two witnesses, relatives or not, who are adults, can sign, and carry a Dominican ID card or, for foreigners, a valid passport. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026): documents are lodged 'en la Oficialía Civil al momento de agendar la fecha del matrimonio' (at the civil registry office when booking the wedding date). On notice, the page only says that for Italian citizens the edict (edicto) must not be waived and must be posted at the Oficialía at least three days before the wedding; it does not state a notice period for other foreigners.

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026), item 7: if the couple will marry under separation of property ('separación de Bienes'), an authentic deed must be given to the civil registry officer, registered and duly notified, executed before the wedding.

JCE help centre (read live 24 November 2026) lists official civil marriage fees ('TASAS'). Between non-resident foreigners: 'Matrimonio Dentro de la Oficialía - Entre Extranjeros No Residentes Legales: RD$25,000.00' and 'Matrimonio Fuera de la Oficialía - Entre Extranjeros No Residentes Legales: RD$25,000.00' (inside or outside the registry office). FOR NIC'S SIGN-OFF ONLY; per brief no prices in the article.

As at November 2026, the Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (mirex.gob.do subdomain; page published 12 February 2015, read live 24 November 2026): 'Las Oficialías del Estado Civil de la República Dominicana asisten a cualquier ciudadano del mundo en el proceso de matrimonio, sin importar que el matrimonio se efectúe entre un extranjero y un dominicano o entre dos extranjeros'. Paraphrase: civil registry offices assist any citizen, including marriages between two foreigners, applying Dominican law. Steps listed: choose an Oficialía del Estado Civil (usually one per municipality), request the requirements, and request a booking date 'para que el Juez Civil efectúe el matrimonio' (for the civil judge to perform the marriage). The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
facts.conflicts: Page dated 2015 and written for a European consulate; JCE page (modified 1 July 2025) is the more current primary source.

facts.claim: Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (read live 24 November 2026), observation 4: 'Existe la posibilidad de que el Juez Civil se traslade, previo acuerdo, al lugar que le indiquen los ciudadanos contrayentes. Por esta flexibilidad muchos matrimonios pueden celebrarse en establecimientos hoteleros'. Paraphrase: by prior arrangement the civil judge can travel to a place the couple nominates, so many marriages take place in hotels. (JCE also lists separate fees for marriage 'Fuera de la Oficialía', outside the registry office.)

Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (read live 24 November 2026): requirements include an apostilled birth certificate for each party, a recent divorce certificate if divorced, an apostilled 'Declaración Jurada de Soltería', passport photocopy, 'Presentarse físicamente al Acto de Ceremonia' (attend the ceremony in person), 'Dos (2) testigos' and 'Dos (2) padrinos ... (mínimo uno)'.
facts.conflicts: Witness wording differs from JCE: JCE says at least two witnesses with ID/passport; this consulate page lists two witnesses plus padrinos (minimum one). Treat JCE as primary; check with the chosen Oficialía.

facts.claim: Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (read live 24 November 2026), note 4: 'Una vez casado, la Oficialía del Estado Civil le entregará un Certificado de Acta de Matrimonio, que para que tenga efecto en el extranjero se recomienda que sea debidamente apostillada en la Cancillería Dominicana.' Paraphrase: after the wedding the registry issues a marriage certificate; for use abroad it is recommended it be apostilled at the Dominican Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (read live 24 November 2026), note 3: if no separation-of-property deed is presented, 'el matrimonio se declarará en Comunidad de Bienes Muebles y Gananciales' (community of movable property and acquests).

Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (read live 24 November 2026), observation 5, quoted only: 'Las leyes de la República Dominicana no prevén el matrimonio de un mismo sexo.' (Dominican law does not provide for same-sex marriage.)

Dominican Consulate General in the Netherlands (read live 24 November 2026), observation 3: 'El precio exacto del servicio se entrega directamente en la Oficialía del Estado Civil elegida.' (exact price is given by the chosen registry office).

The WMO World Weather Information Service publishes climatological normals for Punta Cana (Dominican Republic) itself, supplied by the Oficina Nacional de Meteorología (ONAMET), the Dominican national meteorological service.

WMO WWIS remarks for Punta Cana: climatological information is based on monthly averages for the 30-year period 1961-1990, and 'mean number of rain days' means the mean number of days with at least 1 mm of rain. WWIS cautions that averaging periods and rain-day definitions may differ between countries, so care is needed when comparing city climatologies.

Per the WMO WWIS Punta Cana table (1961-1990), mean daily maximum temperatures are lowest in February (27.6 C) and January (27.7 C) and highest in September (30.9 C) and August (30.7 C).

Per the WMO WWIS Punta Cana table (1961-1990), the wettest month by mean rainfall is October (152.1 mm, 11.4 rain days) followed by May (124.4 mm); the driest are February and March (54.2 mm each, 6.8 and 6.7 rain days).
US National Hurricane Center: 'The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30.' The Atlantic basin includes the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea and Gulf of America.

US National Hurricane Center: tropical cyclone activity sometimes occurs before and after the official June 1 to November 30 season; the peak of the Atlantic hurricane season is September 10, with most activity occurring between mid-August and mid-October.

US National Hurricane Center: based on the 1991-2020 climate period, an average Atlantic season has 14 named storms, 7 hurricanes and 3 major hurricanes; formation dates in individual seasons can vary considerably from the averages.

insider_details.detail: Australian documents for a Dominican civil wedding need an apostille and, because they are in English, a Spanish translation by a judicial interpreter legalised in the Dominican Republic; build several months into the timeline for apostilles and translation. Phrase as planning advice and have the Wedded Advisor confirm current requirements.

The civil judge can travel to a resort by prior arrangement, and JCE publishes a separate 'outside the registry office' fee schedule, so a legal ceremony at the resort itself is possible on the official sources; book the judge's date with the Oficialía early.
Witnesses must be adults who can sign and carry a valid passport; plan for two guests to bring their passports to the ceremony.

Ask the Oficialía about property regime: without a separation-of-property deed signed before the wedding, the marriage is recorded under community of property. Couples should take their own legal advice.
After the wedding, get the Dominican marriage certificate apostilled for use in Australia; Australia won't register it, and some states may not accept it for a name change.

Australia has no embassy in the Dominican Republic; the Embassy of Canada in Santo Domingo and the Australian Embassy in Mexico provide consular help, so carry certified passport copies and keep originals of wedding documents secure.

For the driest, mildest wedding weather, the official Punta Cana normals point to February and March: about 54 mm of rain and fewer than 7 rain days a month, with average highs around 27.6 to 28.1 C. Plan outdoor ceremonies in this window if the guest list allows.

October is the wettest month in the official record (152.1 mm over about 11 rain days) and sits inside the NHC's mid-August to mid-October peak of hurricane activity. A September or October date needs a confirmed indoor or covered rain plan and flexible guest travel insurance.

Even in the hottest months (August and September) mean daily highs sit around 30.7 to 30.9 C, so the issue is humidity and sun rather than extreme heat. Schedule outdoor ceremonies for late afternoon and build shade and water stations into the run sheet (planning advice, not a sourced fact).

Every guest must complete the Dominican Republic's electronic entry and exit form and buy a tourist card on arrival (valid 30 days, per Smartraveller as at November 2026). Put both in the guest travel pack early; the Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements before you book.
Book group airport transfers with official or pre-arranged operators and land guests in daylight where possible, as Smartraveller advises daylight airport travel and warns against unofficial taxis.
Tell guests to bring US dollars rather than Australian dollars for tips and incidentals, since Smartraveller says AUD can't be exchanged for Dominican pesos.
